doctrine.summary: Video tutorial collection covering AI tooling, automation opportunity identification, and developer toolchain setup. Primary value is in named frameworks and tactical numbers from segments 1-20. Final segments (21-30) are GitHub repo documentation with near-zero instructional content.

core_frameworks.name: DMAIC / Lean Six Sigma for AI Automation Scoping
core_frameworks.application: Use DMAIC (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control) to identify where AI automation has highest ROI. Key stat: 40% waste in most manual business processes is the threshold signal. Apply to client intake, retouching queues, outreach sequences, booking workflows before automating.

core_frameworks.name: 3-Step Rapid App Build Pattern (APPA method)
core_frameworks.application: Define input/output → pick AI model → connect UI. Target: 2-3 minute functional prototype. Useful for internal SNIPED tooling (gallery intake forms, shoot-day checklists, VIB intake) before committing to full-stack build.

core_frameworks.name: Google AI Studio Free Tier Web App Pattern
core_frameworks.application: Build lightweight web apps against Gemini API at zero cost for prototyping. Viable path for SNIPED internal tools before Vercel/paid hosting is justified.

core_frameworks.name: OpenClaw Security Hardening (10-Step)
core_frameworks.application: When deploying Claude/AI agent infrastructure: (1) scope permissions minimally, (2) sanitize inputs, (3) rate-limit API calls, (4) log all tool invocations, (5) rotate keys on schedule, (6) isolate agent environments, (7) audit third-party plugins, (8) enforce output filtering, (9) test adversarial prompts, (10) run staged rollouts. Apply before exposing any SNIPED AI agent to client-facing surfaces.

core_frameworks.name: QA Sampling Rate Doctrine
core_frameworks.application: 1-10% QA sampling is the validated industry floor for automated AI output pipelines. Do not ship AI-generated assets (composites, captions, outreach) without spot-checking at minimum 1-in-10.

tactical_numbers: 40% waste threshold: signals a process is worth automating
95% failure rate on AI automations that skip scoping (DMAIC reduces this)
2-3 minutes: target build time for MVP internal app with APPA
1-10%: QA sampling floor for automated AI output
tool_patterns: Claude / OpenClaw: skill integration via MCP; security hardening before production use
Google AI Studio: free Gemini API access for prototyping web apps
APPA: rapid business app builder, no-code to low-code, 2-3 min prototypes
GitHub repo patterns (segments 21-30): Taste Skill, Impeccable, awesome-design-md — reference-level only, not instructional
what_to_ignore: Segments 21-30: GitHub repo README content (OpenClaw, Taste Skill, Impeccable, awesome-design-md) — 95% boilerplate, install docs, contributor lists. No teaching methodology.
UI walkthrough narration throughout — step-by-step screen navigation has zero reusable doctrine.
doctrine.routing_notes: Lean Six Sigma / DMAIC frame applies directly to SNIPED automation decisions (retouching pipeline, outreach sequencing, gallery delivery). Security hardening checklist applies before any OpenClaw/MCP agent goes client-facing. QA sampling rate is a hard floor for any AI-generated deliverable in the SNIPED pipeline.

notes: 30-segment doc; segments 1-20 carry the instructional payload. Segments 21-30 are repo documentation, not course content. Classified as transcript (video tutorial transcripts) with medium signal: frameworks and numbers are real and usable, but buried in heavy UI narration boilerplate. No identity-locking content; pure tooling/methodology.
